claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: TdTomato+ axon patterns in control E15.5 embryos corresponded closely with the pattern of developing 5-HT-labeled axons in the ventral and lateral funiculi of the spinal cord.
claims.source: TdTomato+ axon patterns in control E15.5 embryos corresponded closely with the pattern of developing 5-HT-labeled axons in the ventral and lateral funiculi of the spinal cord, thus indicating specific labeling of descending 5-HT axons with TdTomato (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The pattern of control TdTomato+ axon distribution throughout the embryonic and adult spinal cord corresponded to descending 5-HT axons patterns described in the rat and mouse.
claims.source: In addition, the pattern of control TdTomato+ axon distribution throughout the embryonic and adult spinal cord corresponded to descending 5-HT axons patterns in gray and white matter described in the rat and mouse with an anti-5-HT antibody (Ballion et al., 2002; Rajaofetra et al., 1989).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and comparison with current data.

claims.claim: The number of TdTomato-labeled Pet1+ neurons in the medullary raphe nuclei did not differ between Lmx1bcKO and control mice at 3 months of age.
claims.source: We confirmed that the number of TdTomato-labeled Pet1+ neurons in the medullary raphe nuclei did not differ between Lmx1bcKO and control mice at 3 months of age (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not express Tph2 in medullary neurons.
claims.source: Further, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not express Tph2, confirming targeting of Lmx1b (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: A severe lack of TdTomato+ axons was found in the white matter funiculi of Lmx1bcKO spinal cords.
claims.source: We found a severe lack of TdTomato+ axons in the white matter funiculi, through which 5-HT axon projections normally extend caudally through the spinal cord (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: A severe reduction of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons was found in gray matter at all levels of the spinal cord.
claims.source: In addition, a severe reduction of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons was found in gray matter at all levels of the spinal cord (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The normally dense innervation to the dorsal and ventral horns of control spinal cords was dramatically decreased in cervical, thoracic and lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO mice.
claims.source: The normally dense innervation to the dorsal and ventral horns of control spinal cords was dramatically decreased in cervical, thoracic and lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C.

claims.claim: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter in Lmx1bcKO mice.
claims.source: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter while at lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claims.claim: At lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter in Lmx1bcKO mice.
claims.source: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter while at lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a 73% deficit at cervical levels in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords.
claims.source: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a progressive cervical to lumbar deficit, 73% and 94%, respectively in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a 94% deficit at lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords.
claims.source: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a progressive cervical to lumbar deficit, 73% and 94%, respectively in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The deficit in 5-HT axons becomes increasingly profound with increasing distance from 5-HT cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice.
claims.source: Collectively, our results indicate that Lmx1b deficiency severely disrupts long-range 5-HT axon architecture in the forebrain and spinal cord and that the deficit becomes increasingly profound with increasing distance from 5-HT cell bodies.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: At E13.5, TdTomato+ axon outgrowth and trajectory in Lmx1bcKO mice were normal as they coursed through the MFB over the mesencephalic flexure.
claims.source: We first investigated TdTomato+ axons at E13.5 when primary pathway formation is underway and Lmx1b conditional targeting has occurred. At this stage, TdTomato+ axon outgrowth and trajectory in Lmx1bcKO mice were normal as they coursed through the MFB over the mesencephalic flexure (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3A.

claims.claim: At E16.5, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons exhibited a clear failure to extend as far rostrally as control axons.
claims.source: At E16.5, however, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons exhibited a clear failure to extend as far rostrally as control axons, suggesting either aborted or delayed axon outgrowth along the more rostral portions of the MFB during late stage primary pathway formation (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claims.claim: At E18.5, the density of control TdTomato+ axons was maximal throughout the MFB.
claims.source: At E18.5, the density of control TdTomato+ axons was maximal throughout the MFB and TdTomato+ axons were present as far rostral as the septum and diagonal band, where 5-HT axons turn dorsally to navigate through the cingulum, supracallosal stria, and fimbria-fornix (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claims.claim: At E18.5, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appeared at normal density throughout the MFB.
claims.source: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons now appeared at normal density throughout the MFB, thus supporting delayed axon outgrowth at E16.5 (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claims.claim: At E18.5, most Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons failed to turn dorsally and remained stalled within the MFB.
claims.source: However, at this stage, most Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons failed to turn dorsally and remained stalled within the MFB.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claims.claim: A smaller number of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did turn dorsally away from the MFB to pass through the septum and diagonal band at E18.5.
claims.source: A smaller number of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did turn dorsally away from the MFB to pass through the septum and diagonal band (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Virtually all Lmx1bcKO axons failed to extend and selectively route into the cingulum and fimbria-fornix at E18.5.
claims.source: Virtually all Lmx1bcKO axons failed to extend and selectively route into the cingulum and fimbria-fornix, thus failing to reach the cortex and hippocampus.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claims.claim: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did not exhibit ectopic trajectories at E18.5.
claims.source: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons still did not exhibit ectopic trajectories.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claims.claim: Conditional targeting of Lmx1b at E12.5 results in delayed primary pathway formation followed by a profound failure of ascending axons to selectively route into pre-existing fiber tracts.
claims.source: These findings suggest that conditional targeting of Lmx1b at E12.5 results in delayed primary pathway formation followed by a profound failure of ascending axons to selectively route into pre-existing fiber tracts.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: At E15.5, TdTomato+ fibers showed similar initial axon outgrowth through the caudal medulla to the upper cervical spinal cord from Lmx1bcKO and control medullary 5-HT cell bodies.
claims.source: Analysis of descending TdTomato+ fibers at E15.5 revealed similar initial axon outgrowth through the caudal medulla to the upper cervical spinal cord from Lmx1bcKO and control medullary 5-HT cell bodies (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Although Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appropriately entered the lateral and ventral funiculi of the cervical spinal cord, greatly reduced densities were evident beginning at mid-cervical levels.
claims.source: Although Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appropriately entered the lateral and ventral funiculi of the cervical spinal cord, greatly reduced densities were evident beginning at mid-cervical levels (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claims.claim: At lumbar levels, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons were nearly undetectable in the lateral and ventral funiculi.
claims.source: At lumbar levels, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons were nearly undetectable in the lateral and ventral funiculi (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claims.claim: TdTomato+ axons were not able to extend into the funiculi, which caused a severe and progressive cervical to lumbar deficit of 5-HT innervation in the adult Lmx1bcKO spinal cord.
claims.source: These results indicate that TdTomato+ axons were not able to extend into the funiculi, which caused a severe and progressive cervical to lumbar deficit of 5-HT innervation in the adult Lmx1bcKO spinal cord (Figures 2 and 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Subcutaneous delivery of tamoxifen into iControl pups resulted in approximately 94% of Tph2+ neurons co-labeled with TdTomato in the DRN/MRN/B9.
claims.source: Subcutaneous delivery of tamoxifen into iControl pups resulted in approximately 94% of Tph2+ neurons co-labeled with TdTomato in the DRN/MRN/B9 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: 94% of TdTomato+ cells were co-labeled with Tph2 in tamoxifen-treated iControl pups.
claims.source: Conversely, 94% of TdTomato+ cells were co-labeled with Tph2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: RT-qPCR analysis verified that Lmx1b mRNA was significantly reduced in Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: RT-qPCR analysis of flow sorted TdTomato+ cells verified that Lmx1b mRNA was significantly reduced in Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Equivalent numbers of TdTomato-labeled cell bodies were generated in Lmx1bicKO versus iControl mice after injection of tamoxifen.
claims.source: Equivalent numbers of TdTomato-labeled cell bodies were generated in Lmx1bicKO versus iControl mice after injection of tamoxifen (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: Cell body size and distribution of tamoxifen treated Lmx1bicKO TdTomato+ cells were not different from that of iControl TdTomato+ cells.
claims.source: In contrast to Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells, cell body size and distribution of tamoxifen treated Lmx1bicKO TdTomato+ cells were not different from that of iControl TdTomato+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E.

claims.claim: A dramatic deficit in TdTomato+ arbors was found throughout the hippocampus in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: We found a dramatic deficit in TdTomato+ arbors throughout the hippocampus in Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C.

claims.claim: TdTomato+ arbors were severely reduced in all layers of the cortex in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: In addition, TdTomato+ arbors were severely reduced in all layers of the cortex with the most medial layers almost completely devoid of arbors in Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Lmx1b is temporally required for postnatal development of 5-HT terminal axons.
claims.source: These results clearly demonstrate that Lmx1b is temporally required for postnatal development of 5-HT terminal axons.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: TdTomato labeling within the supracallosal stria and cingulum was consistently less intense in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls.
claims.source: However, we noticed that in addition to reduced 5-HT arbors in the hippocampus and cortex, TdTomato labeling within the supracallosal stria and cingulum, major routes to the hippocampus and cortex, were consistently less intense in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4C, asterisk).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Major 5-HT routes (supracallosal stria and cingulum) had not yet fully formed in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: Indeed, further detailed examination revealed that these major 5-HT routes had not yet fully formed (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Quantification confirmed a significant decrease in TdTomato+ axons within the cingulum and supracallosal stria tracts in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls.
claims.source: Quantification of TdTomato+ axons within the cingulum and supracallosal stria tracts confirmed a significant decrease in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period.
claims.source: These results indicate that i, long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period and ii, Lmx1b is required at this stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Lmx1b is required at the P1 stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
claims.source: These results indicate that i, long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period and ii, Lmx1b is required at this stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: The density of TdTomato-labeled fibers in the supracallosal stria was similar in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.
claims.source: Importantly, in contrast to findings obtained in P1 targeted mice, we found that the density of TdTomato-labeled fibers in the supracallosal stria was now similar in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: TdTomato-labeled fibers in the cingulum were comparable in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.

claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Quantification confirmed no significant difference in the cingulum and supracallosal stria between P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.
claims.source: Quantification of the cingulum and supracallosal stria confirmed no significant difference between P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: 5-HT axon routing was complete in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: These findings indicate that 5-HT axon routing was complete in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: TdTomato+ arbors were significantly decreased throughout the hippocampus in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: Despite fully developed 5-HT selective pathway routes in the forebrain, TdTomato+ arbors were significantly decreased throughout the hippocampus (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: A majority of remaining arbors detected within the hippocampus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice were found in the molecular layer (SLM).
claims.source: A majority of remaining arbors detected within the hippocampus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice were found in the molecular layer (SLM), which are the first 5-HT arbors to appear in the hippocampus during rat development (Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: TdTomato+ arbors were severely decreased in all cortical layers of the P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO brain.
claims.source: TdTomato+ arbors were also severely decreased in all cortical layers of the P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO brain including in layer I and VI where axons of passage also exist (Figure 5D) (Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D and a citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: Quantification confirmed a significant decrease of TdTomato+ axon arbors in the cortex of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO compared to iControls.
claims.source: Quantification of the cortex confirmed a significant decrease of TdTomato+ axon arbors in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO compared to iControls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Many 5-HT terminal arbors have already been generated in the forebrain at P3.
claims.source: It is important to note that many 5-HT terminal arbors have already been generated in the forebrain at P3 (Lidov and Molliver, 1982; Maddaloni et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: Lmx1b targeting at P3 results in the failure of new arbors to form while leaving previously generated arbors intact.
claims.source: Thus, Lmx1b targeting at P3 results in the failure of new arbors to form while leaving previously generated arbors intact.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: Arborization deficits were found within the thalamus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: Interestingly, arborization deficits were also found within the thalamus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claims.claim: The normally dense arborization within the PVT was absent in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
claims.source: Similar to what we observed in Lmx1bcKO mice, the normally dense arborization within the PVT was absent in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice, rendering the PVT indiscernible (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5E.

claims.claim: Lmx1b switches to control terminal arborization of forebrain 5-HT axons at a successive stage.
claims.source: Together, these results reveal a successive stage of continuous Lmx1b function during which it switches to control terminal arborization of forebrain 5-HT axons.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claims.claim: The numbers of TdTomato+ cells in each raphe nuclei did not differ in Tph2cKO and control mice.
claims.source: The numbers of TdTomato+ cells in each raphe nuclei did not differ in Tph2cKO and control mice (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6A.

claims.claim: A 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons was found in Tph2cKO mice in the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei.
claims.source: In the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei, we found a 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Tph2cKO compared to the 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 6B,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B,C.

claims.claim: A 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons was found in Lmx1bcKO mice in the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei.
claims.source: In the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei, we found a 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Tph2cKO compared to the 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 6B,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B,C.

claims.claim: Loss of 5-HT itself was confirmed in Tph2cKO mice.

results.result: Lmx1b-deficient 5-HT neurons fail to generate proper axonal projections to the forebrain. While TdTomato+ axons are present in normal density within the MFB, they are nearly completely missing throughout the forebrain distal to the thalamus, failing to reach fiber tracts and target regions including the olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, and striatum. In the thalamus, aberrant clumping and absence of arbors in specific regions (including the PVT) are observed.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C32-C39 provide converging anatomical evidence from multiple forebrain regions showing severe deficits in 5-HT axon projections in Lmx1bcKO mice. The data are supported by immunohistochemistry, fluorescent imaging, and viral tracing (C40-C41), with appropriate controls and multiple anatomical levels examined. The phenotype is consistent and well-documented across figures.

results.result: Lmx1b-deficient 5-HT neurons fail to generate proper descending axonal projections to the spinal cord. Severe deficits in TdTomato+ axons are found in both white matter funiculi and gray matter at all spinal cord levels, with progressive cervical to lumbar deficits (67-92% in white matter, 73-94% in gray matter). The deficit becomes increasingly profound with increasing distance from 5-HT cell bodies.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C55 and C68 provide quantitative and qualitative evidence for descending pathway deficits. The progressive rostral-to-caudal gradient of deficits is well-documented with quantification at multiple spinal levels (C51-C54). The data are supported by appropriate imaging and statistical analysis (two-way ANOVA mentioned in methods).

results.result: Developmental analysis reveals that Lmx1b deficiency causes delayed primary pathway formation (E13.5-E18.5) followed by profound failure of ascending axons to selectively route into pre-existing fiber tracts. At E13.5, axon outgrowth and trajectory are normal, but by E16.5, axons fail to extend as far rostrally as controls. By E18.5, most mutant axons fail to turn dorsally and remain stalled in the MFB, failing to route into the cingulum and fimbria-fornix.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C64 provide temporal analysis of axon development at multiple embryonic stages (E13.5, E16.5, E18.5) with appropriate imaging. The progression from normal initial outgrowth to delayed extension to routing failure is logically documented. The absence of ectopic trajectories (C63) strengthens the interpretation of a routing rather than guidance defect.

results.result: Developmental analysis of descending projections shows that while initial axon outgrowth through the caudal medulla to upper cervical spinal cord is similar between Lmx1bcKO and controls at E15.5, mutant axons show greatly reduced densities beginning at mid-cervical levels and are nearly undetectable at lumbar levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C67 provide embryonic analysis of descending pathway development with appropriate temporal resolution. The data show normal initial outgrowth but progressive failure of extension, consistent with the adult phenotype. Imaging evidence is provided in Figure 3D.

results.result: Stage-specific temporal targeting demonstrates that Lmx1b is required at successive stages to control 5-HT axon primary outgrowth, selective routing, and terminal arborization. P1 targeting reveals that long-range 5-HT axon routing continues to develop in the early neonatal period and Lmx1b is required for completion of selective routing. P3 targeting shows Lmx1b switches function to control terminal arborization of forebrain 5-HT axons.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C76, C80-C81, C94 are supported by tamoxifen-inducible targeting experiments at P1 and P3 (C69-C89). The P1 targeting shows incomplete formation of major routes (C77-C79), while P3 targeting shows complete routes but deficient arborization (C82-C89). This temporal dissection provides strong evidence for stage-specific Lmx1b functions. RT-qPCR confirms targeting efficiency (C71).

results.result: Loss of Tph2 and reduced 5-HT levels do not contribute to the routing or arborization defects observed in Lmx1b-deficient mice. Tph2cKO mice show comparable Tph2 reduction (74%) to Lmx1bcKO mice (79%) and confirmed loss of 5-HT, but display normal TdTomato+ axon patterns throughout the forebrain and spinal cord.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C101 provide critical control experiments demonstrating that the axon phenotypes are not secondary to loss of 5-HT synthesis. The Tph2cKO mice show comparable Tph2 reduction to Lmx1bcKO mice (C96-C97) with confirmed 5-HT loss (C98), but normal axon patterns (C99-C100). This strongly supports a direct role for Lmx1b in axon development independent of its role in 5-HT synthesis.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis reveals that Lmx1b controls expression of hundreds of genes in rostral and caudal 5-HT neurons, with strong enrichment for axon development genes. In rostral neurons, 784 genes are decreased and 118 increased; in caudal neurons, 1529 genes are decreased and 772 increased. Gene Ontology analysis shows the top enriched term is axon development (>150 genes, BH-adjusted p=0), with 422 total axon-related genes regulated by Lmx1b. Many genes are uniquely regulated in rostral vs. caudal neurons, suggesting distinct axonal regulatory programs.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C115 are supported by comprehensive RNA-seq analysis with appropriate bioinformatics (differential expression, GO enrichment). The data show robust changes in gene expression with strong statistical support (FDR ≤ 0.05). The enrichment for axon development genes provides molecular support for the anatomical phenotypes. Sample sizes (n=3 controls, n=2 Lmx1bcKO) are modest but acceptable for RNA-seq. RT-qPCR validation is provided for some genes (C116, Figure 7O).

results.result: Pet1 is required for forebrain but not spinal cord 5-HT pathway formation, revealing distinct transcription factor requirements for ascending vs. descending projections. Pet1cKO mice show normal spinal cord axon patterns but severe deficits in forebrain regions (olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, striatum, hypothalamus) with disrupted thalamic patterns, while maintaining normal density in the MFB.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C125 provide strong evidence for subsystem-specific transcriptional control. The contrast between normal spinal cord (C118-C120) and severely deficient forebrain (C121-C123) in Pet1cKO mice is well-documented with quantification and imaging. This demonstrates that the Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade operates specifically in the ascending system. Pet1 transcript loss is confirmed by ISH (mentioned in text).

results.result: The Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade is temporally required for 5-HT arborization and controls upregulation of Protocadherin-alphac2 (Pcdhac2) during postnatal development. Lmx1b continues to control Pet1 postnatally (C137), and both factors co-regulate 15 axon-related genes including Pcdhac2 (C138-C140). Pcdhac2 is significantly upregulated only at the onset of arborization (C145) and both Lmx1b and Pet1 are required for its postnatal upregulation (C147-C148).
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C137-C149 provide molecular evidence for the Lmx1b→Pet1→Pcdhac2 regulatory cascade. The temporal control is demonstrated by: (1) continued Pet1 regulation by Lmx1b postnatally (C137, RT-qPCR and ISH), (2) co-regulation of Pcdhac2 by both factors (C143, differential exon analysis), (3) stage-specific upregulation of Pcdhac2 (C145, time-series RNA-seq), and (4) requirement for both factors in postnatal Pcdhac2 upregulation (C147-C148, ISH at P14). This provides a mechanistic link between transcription factors and a known effector of 5-HT arborization.

results.result: ChIP-seq analysis identifies Pet1 binding sites in the Pcdhac2 locus, suggesting direct regulation. Two significant mycPet1 peaks are found: one at the 5' end of the unique Pcdhac2 first exon (lacking a Pet1 motif match) and one within the third-intronic DNase I hypersensitivity site HS7 (containing a significant Pet1 motif match).
results.evaluation: Claims C150-C154 provide ChIP-seq evidence for direct Pet1 binding to the Pcdhac2 locus. The identification of two peaks with one containing a significant Pet1 motif match (C154) supports direct regulation. The HS7 site is a well-characterized enhancer (C152, with citations), strengthening the functional interpretation. However, the lack of a Pet1 motif at the TSS peak (C153) suggests potential indirect binding or co-factor involvement at that site.

results.result: Postnatal temporal targeting of Pet1 demonstrates that the Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade operates continually over an extended postnatal period to control stage-specific gene expression and generate both early and late 5-HT terminal arbor patterns. P3 targeting shows severe deficits in hippocampus and cortex (C155), while P5 targeting reveals deficits in the striatum (C156), a late-developing region.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C157 are supported by tamoxifen-inducible Pet1 targeting at P3 and P5. The P3 Pet1icKO phenotype mirrors the P3 Lmx1bicKO phenotype (C155), supporting the cascade model. The P5 targeting showing striatal deficits (C156) demonstrates continued requirement for Pet1 in late-developing regions. This temporal analysis strengthens the conclusion of stage-specific control.

results.result: While Pet1cKO largely phenocopies Lmx1bcKO forebrain defects, distinct differences in thalamic patterns suggest that Lmx1b→Pet1 is the main regulatory program but additional minor Lmx1b- or Pet1-orchestrated pathways operate. Pet1cKO thalamus shows different clumping patterns and normal PVT arborization (unlike Lmx1bcKO), suggesting Lmx1b may act independently of Pet1 in the PVT.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C129 and C132 identify subtle but important differences between Pet1cKO and Lmx1bcKO phenotypes, particularly in the thalamus. The normal PVT patterning in Pet1cKO (C128) contrasts with its absence in Lmx1bcKO (C39), supporting Pet1-independent Lmx1b functions. This nuanced analysis strengthens the overall model by acknowledging complexity beyond a simple linear cascade.

results.result: Validation of the genetic labeling strategy shows that in control mice, 82% of Tph2+ neurons express TdTomato and 88% of TdTomato+ cells express Tph2, with TdTomato+ axons colocalizing with 5-HT and matching previously described 5-HT axon patterns. In Lmx1bcKO mice, equivalent numbers of TdTomato+ cell bodies are present and remain stable for at least 13 months, though they are smaller and do not express Lmx1b or Tph2.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C31 provide essential validation of the genetic labeling approach and confirm successful Lmx1b targeting. The Pet1-Cre efficiency is well-characterized (C20-C21), TdTomato labeling is validated against 5-HT and previous literature (C23-C25), and Lmx1b targeting is confirmed by loss of Lmx1b and Tph2 expression (C27-C28). Cell survival is documented (C29-C30), ruling out cell death as an explanation for axon deficits. This is critical methodological validation.

results.result: Validation of genetic labeling in the medullary 5-HT system shows that in control animals, 80% of Tph2+ medullary cell bodies express TdTomato and 92% of TdTomato+ cells express Tph2, with TdTomato+ axon patterns corresponding to previously described descending 5-HT axon patterns. In Lmx1bcKO mice, equivalent numbers of TdTomato+ neurons are present but do not express Tph2.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C47 provide validation of the labeling strategy for the descending system, parallel to the validation for the ascending system. The efficiency is comparable (80-92%) and patterns match literature descriptions (C44-C45). Successful targeting is confirmed by loss of Tph2 (C47). This validates the approach for studying descending projections.

results.result: Validation of the tamoxifen-inducible targeting strategy shows that subcutaneous tamoxifen delivery results in approximately 94% co-labeling of Tph2+ neurons with TdTomato in iControl pups, with RT-qPCR verification of Lmx1b mRNA reduction in Lmx1bicKO mice. Equivalent numbers of TdTomato+ cell bodies are generated in Lmx1bicKO vs. iControl mice, with normal cell body size and distribution.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C73 validate the tamoxifen-inducible approach with high efficiency (94%, C69-C70) and confirmed targeting (C71, RT-qPCR). The normal cell body size and distribution in tamoxifen-treated mice (C73) contrasts with the smaller size in constitutive Lmx1bcKO mice (C31), suggesting the size difference may be a developmental consequence of early Lmx1b loss rather than a direct effect. This is important methodological validation.

results.result: Early Pet1 deficiency does not result in reduced cell body size, demonstrating that reduced cell body size in Lmx1bcKO mice did not contribute to the axon defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C130-C131 provide an important control showing that cell body size reduction is not responsible for axon defects. Since Pet1cKO mice have normal cell body size (C130) but similar forebrain axon defects to Lmx1bcKO mice, the smaller cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice (C31) are unlikely to explain the axon phenotype. This strengthens the interpretation of direct effects on axon development.

results.result: Analysis of double knockout (DKO) mice shows that simultaneous loss of Lmx1b and Pet1 does not produce more severe deficits than Lmx1bcKO alone. DKO spinal cords show similar deficits to Lmx1bcKO, and DKO forebrain does not show more extreme deficits than Lmx1bcKO, with the DKO thalamus mirroring the Lmx1bcKO phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C135 provide genetic epistasis analysis showing that Pet1 does not compensate for Lmx1b loss. The lack of additive effects in DKO mice supports a model where Pet1 acts downstream of Lmx1b in the ascending system. The similar phenotypes between DKO and Lmx1bcKO (C133-C135) are consistent with the proposed regulatory cascade.

results.result: Analysis of Pet1-/- embryos carrying the Pet1-YFP transgene shows comparable initial 5-HT primary axon outgrowth in Pet1-/- and control 5-HT neuron cell bodies at E13.5.
results.evaluation: Claim C136 addresses whether the initial 1-2 days of Pet1 expression (not targeted by Pet1-Cre) is required for primary pathway formation. The comparable initial outgrowth in Pet1-/- embryos (C136) suggests Pet1 is not required for axon initiation, consistent with the Pet1cKO phenotype showing normal MFB axons (C123). This is a useful control but represents a single timepoint observation.

results.result: AAV2 viral injection into the DRN/MRN confirms the absence of YFP+ axons in all distal forebrain areas where TdTomato+ axons are absent in Lmx1bcKO mice, with YFP+ axons colocalizing with TdTomato+ axons in all forebrain areas.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C41 provide independent validation of the axon deficit using viral tracing. The colocalization of YFP and TdTomato in areas where axons are present (C41) and absence in areas lacking TdTomato (C40) confirms that the TdTomato labeling accurately reflects the axon deficit. This is important methodological validation ruling out artifacts of the genetic reporter.

results.result: Background information on the 5-HT system establishes that 5-HT modulates nearly all neural circuitry despite being produced in a small population of neurons, achieves expansive neuromodulation through long-range diffuse projections, and develops through three successive stages (primary pathway formation, selective routing, terminal arborization). Lmx1b is a crucial factor in 5-HT gene regulatory networks, controlling Tph2 and Slc6a4 expression, with its loss resulting in extremely low 5-HT levels and various behavioral phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C19 provide essential background context supported by appropriate citations to previous literature. These claims establish the biological significance of the 5-HT system, the developmental stages being studied, and prior knowledge of Lmx1b function. While these are not novel findings from this study, they provide necessary context and are accurately cited.

results.result: Background information on 5-HT arbor development and Pcdhac2 function establishes that many 5-HT terminal arbors have already been generated at P3, and that Pcdhac2 has a key intrinsic role in 5-HT axon arbor formation and patterning, with Pcdhac2-deficient mice exhibiting lack of forebrain arbors and severe clumping. Previous work showed Pcdhac2 was not significantly regulated by Pet1 at earlier stages.
results.evaluation: Claims C90, C141-C142, C144 provide important background context for interpreting the Pcdhac2 findings. The prior knowledge that arbors are already present at P3 (C90) helps interpret the P3 targeting results. The established role of Pcdhac2 in arborization (C141-C142) and its lack of early Pet1 regulation (C144) provide context for the novel finding of postnatal regulation. These are accurately cited background claims.

results.result: The overall conclusion that a single continuously expressed transcription factor, Lmx1b, functions at successive stages to orchestrate the progressive development of long-range axon architectures enabling expansive neuromodulation.
results.evaluation: Claim C158 represents the main conclusion synthesizing all major findings. It is well-supported by the collective evidence showing: (1) Lmx1b deficiency disrupts multiple stages of axon development (C1, C48, C64, C68), (2) temporal targeting reveals stage-specific requirements (C2, C76, C80-C81, C94), (3) Lmx1b controls expression of hundreds of axon-related genes (C109-C111), and (4) the Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade operates temporally to control stage-specific genes like Pcdhac2 (C3-C4, C149, C157). This is a major integrative conclusion.
